description: Where can Q_beta be real with Im(q) != 0? Under BOTH complex extensions of the closed form the solution set is y=0 plus one non-real branch, and the substrate Re(q)=q_0 lies in neither branch -- so on the substrate, Im(Q_beta)=0 forces Im(q)=0. Corrects bean qou-c66b's stronger unqualified claim, and closes conj:im-q-physical-role candidate (ii) using an observable the framework already has -- and not merely at q_0: the CAL-2 Apollonius circle that candidate (ii) posits as its admissible set lies ENTIRELY in Re(q) > 1/2 (leftmost 0.909850, margin 0.410), so every non-real point of the arc is excluded and only its two real intersections survive.
engine: sympy (exact symbolic over ZZ[x,y]) + mpmath 50 dps spot-checks; no float64
q0AnchorReason: AGENTS.md 2026-08-07 owner directive: proton is the default for all new compute; this probe is neither an explicit proton-vs-muon comparison (E1) nor an ideal-CAL statement (E2)

data.E2_form: |Delta(net)| * E_0,  Delta(net) = h(h-2)/2, h = q - 1/q, E_0 = m_e/(q(q-1))

cal2_apollonius_circle.reading: CAL-2 with a modulus, |1 - 1/q| = sqrt(k), which is what produces a circle at all; k = Vol(4_1)/(m_mu/m_e)

data.scope: (b) -- structural exclusion citing a proved algebraic identity (the exact factorisation of Im, and the sign of y^2 on the substrate branch), not a numerical near-miss. Scoped to the ARCHIMEDEAN evaluation; AGENTS.md's fibre-vs-observable banner leaves Im(q) unconstrained at the fibre level and this does not touch that.
data.does_not_close: candidate (i), chirality. Nor does it fix WHICH complex extension is canonical -- it shows the substrate answer does not depend on that choice.
data.corrects: bean qou-c66b asserted 'Requiring Im Q_beta = 0 therefore forces Im q = 0' without qualification. One real equation on two real unknowns has a curve of solutions, not a point; the non-real branch is non-empty under both readings. The claim holds on the substrate branch Re(q) > 1/2, and that is where it needed to hold.

assertions.name: substrate_not_in_E1_non_real_branch
assertions.detail: E1 needs Re(q) in Union(Interval.open(-3/2, 0), Interval.open(0, 1/2)); q_0 = 1.10998 > 1/2, so y^2 < 0

assertions.name: modulus_factor_zeros_are_real
assertions.detail: q^2-2q-1 = 0 at [1 - sqrt(2), 1 + sqrt(2)], both real -- no complex escape

assertions.name: the_two_extensions_disagree_off_the_substrate
assertions.detail: E1's open strip and E2's line x=1/2 are disjoint; they agree only that the substrate is excluded -- which is why the conclusion survives qou-c66b's unresolved extension choice

assertions.name: numeric_control_E2_vanishes_on_its_own_locus
assertions.detail: at q = 1/2 + 0.3i, Im(Q_beta) under E2 is 0 to 1e-40 -- the test can see a real Q_beta at complex q when there is one

assertions.name: apollonius_circle_reproduces_the_conjectures_own_numbers
assertions.detail: derived centre 1.00991452125 / radius 0.100064074391 against the conjecture's stated ~1.010 / ~0.100 -- so the modulus reading of CAL-2 used here IS the conjecture's reading

assertions.name: entire_cal2_admissible_set_lies_in_Re_q_gt_half
assertions.detail: leftmost point of the circle is Re(q) = 0.909850446861, a margin of 0.40985045 above 1/2 -- so both branches are empty on the WHOLE arc, not merely near q_0, and candidate (ii)'s test is answered on its entire admissible set

assertions.name: numeric_control_E1_nonzero_off_its_locus
assertions.detail: at q = q_0 + 1e-3 i, Im(Q_beta) under E1 is not 0 -- the test can see a non-real Q_beta too
